messages:
maya: heads up — CI kept flagging the json-telemetry eval as FAILED on quantized-ggml bringup, but local runs look fine. Dashboard shows spike in schema-violations metric at 03:12 UTC. :thinking:

ci-bot: Test job `eval/json-telemetry/ndjson-validate` failed 3x in the last 2 hours. Logs: https://ci.redwood.internal/12345 — see last 200 lines.

alex: any repro steps? stack trace? can you paste the validator log snippet?

maya: pasted the failing chunk below — looks like partial streaming broke the JSON parse when model emitted streaming toolcalls.

maya: ```
ERROR: json.decoder.JSONDecodeError: Unterminated string starting at: line 1 column 345 (char 344)
-- received chunk: '{"call": "invoke_tool", "args": {"id": "fetch_user", "params": {"user_id": 123'
```

jamie: ahhh streaming partial token boundaries. Our validator assumes full payload per example. When quantized model emits chunked function calls we occasionally get NDJSON lines split across TCP frames -> parse error. Repro: run runner with small chunk_size and simulated latency.

samir: btw the metric that increments is `eval.schema.errors.v1` which our dashboard treats as hard regression. For quantized experiments we see ~0.7% of cases where stream chopping happens — traffic pattern dependent.

elaine: that inflated the regression alert yesterday and triggered an oncall ping. We need CI-level fix so flaky parse doesn't count as a metric error; and a dashboard filter for streaming-mode tests.

alex: proposal: change validator to accumulate chunks until braces balance OR detect NDJSON framing (newline delimited). Fallback: if parse fails, buffer up to N ms/bytes then retry. Also mark those incidents as "partial_stream" so metric can be labeled and not counted as a schema regression.

jamie: +1. Minimal patch I tried locally (pseudo):
```python
# accumulate chunked streaming for NDJSON lines
buffer = ""
for chunk in stream:
    buffer += chunk
    while "\n" in buffer:
        line, buffer = buffer.split("\n", 1)
        if not line.strip():
            continue
        try:
            obj = json.loads(line)
        except json.JSONDecodeError:
            # put back and wait for more data
            buffer = line + "\n" + buffer
            break
        handle(obj)
```

samir: can we make this change in the eval runner and also add CI gating that retries the validator job up to 2x before incrementing `eval.schema.errors.v1`? That reduces noise.

maya: sounds good. I'll open a PR for runner patch + unit tests that simulate chunk boundaries. Will also add a small integration in CI: if validator fails with JSONDecodeError, wait 1s, re-run the validator against the job artifacts, then only mark metric if still failing.

elaine: also add an annotation in the dashboard to exclude tests labeled `streaming=true` from the regression alert or lower their weight. I'll coordinate with infra to add label.

alex: one nit — ensure we don't accidentally swallow real malformed outputs (toolcall that is missing required fields). So label must distinguish between "partial_parse" vs "schema_mismatch". The latter should still count.

maya: yep plan: detect incomplete frame (unbalanced braces or trailing partial token) -> tag `partial_parse`. If parse succeeds but schema.validate fails -> `schema_mismatch`. Both emitted to metrics but only `schema_mismatch` increments the alert counter.

samir: will update the telemetry docs for the new tags. Also add a small dashboard widget showing partial vs schema_mismatch counts over time; that should help debug quantized vs model regressions.

ci-bot: Created issue #DEV-7899 for runner patch and CI retry. Linked PR: https://git.redwood/internal/pulls/9876

maya: thanks — assigning to me for the runner change and to elaine for dashboard. I'll drop a short repro gist in the PR. :thumbsup:

alex: great. once PR is in, let's run the quantized-ggml nightly with increased chunking to verify.

jamie: I'll add the unit tests to the eval harness to simulate the streaming edge cases.

maya: ok marking this thread resolved for now, will update when PR merges.
